title: SupTech, Data and Supervisory Analytics
summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors and leaders to govern supervisory data, interrogate returns, use analytics to surface risk and build the authority's SupTech capability.
intro: This training programme equips supervisory staff and leaders to turn regulatory data into supervisory insight: building and governing the authority's data infrastructure, interrogating returns critically, and adopting SupTech tools that genuinely improve risk detection and judgement.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give supervisors and managers a practical understanding of the data, infrastructure and analytical tools that underpin modern risk-based supervision, and of the governance needed to rely on them. Participants leave able to challenge the quality of the evidence behind supervisory decisions, use analytics to surface risk and shape the authority's SupTech roadmap.
sections.What It Covers: SupTech and the data-driven authority, supervisory data infrastructure, data governance and lineage, regulatory reporting and data collection, interrogating regulatory returns, anomaly detection and dashboards, advanced analytics and AI, SupTech use cases across functions, building SupTech capability, and governing supervisory analytics.
Intended Audience: Supervisors and analysts who use regulatory returns, risk scores and dashboards in their day-to-day work
Data, statistics, IT and SupTech teams building the authority's data and analytics capability
Heads of department and senior managers responsible for supervisory strategy, resourcing and technology investment
Learning Objectives: Explain how data infrastructure and SupTech support risk-based supervision across functions
Assess the quality, lineage and governance of the data behind supervisory decisions
Apply trend, peer and anomaly analysis to interrogate regulatory returns
Evaluate advanced analytics and AI tools for supervisory use, including their limits
Assess build-versus-buy, procurement, skills and resourcing choices for SupTech
Design a phased SupTech and data roadmap for the authority
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a briefing with case studies and practical exercises using sample data, and modules can be selected or tailored for supervisors, data teams or senior managers.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of financial supervision or working with regulatory data is helpful. No programming or data science background is required.
Core Reading: BIS Financial Stability Institute, Innovative Technology in Financial Supervision (Suptech): The Experience of Early Users (FSI Insights No 9, 2018)
FSB, The Use of Supervisory and Regulatory Technology by Authorities and Regulated Institutions (2020)
Basel Committee, Principles for Effective Risk Data Aggregation and Risk Reporting (BCBS 239) (2013)

modules.title: SupTech, RegTech and the Data-Driven Authority
modules.summary: What SupTech is, how it differs from firms' RegTech, and why the quality of an authority's evidence base increasingly determines the quality of its supervisory judgement.
objectives: Explain SupTech and RegTech and how they interact
Identify the main categories of SupTech tools and their purposes
Assess realistic expectations of what SupTech can and cannot do
syllabus: SupTech versus RegTech: whose tools and whose data
Categories: data collection, analytics, reporting automation and surveillance
International experience: BIS, FSB and authority surveys
The link between data quality and supervisory judgement

modules.title: Building Supervisory Data Infrastructure
modules.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' understanding of the data and case-management infrastructure that underpins risk-based supervision, and to develop practical skills for evaluating and improving that infrastructure across functions.
objectives: Explain the role of data infrastructure in risk-based supervision
Describe the components of a supervisory case-management system
Assess data integration challenges across supervisory functions
Evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of a sample data architecture
Identify priorities for improving supervisory data infrastructure
syllabus: The link between data quality and supervisory judgement
Core components: case management, risk scoring, document repositories
Common data infrastructure failure modes
Data infrastructure maturity models
Facilitated discussion: how data gaps have affected participants' own supervisory work
Why data silos form between authorisation, supervision and enforcement
Integrating financial crime, prudential and conduct data
Data standards and taxonomies
The cost of poor integration: duplicated effort, missed risk signals
Group exercise: map data flows across a sample authority's functions and identify silos
Evaluating a data architecture against maturity benchmarks
Prioritising improvements given resource constraints
Build versus buy considerations
Case study: a sample authority's data infrastructure
Case study: evaluate a sample architecture and propose a prioritised improvement plan
Recap: infrastructure components, integration, prioritisation
Reflection and discussion
Q&A

modules.title: Data Governance for Supervisory Decision-Making
modules.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' understanding of data governance principles and their application to supervisory decision-making, ensuring that decisions are supported by reliable, well-governed data.
objectives: Explain the principles of good data governance
Describe common data quality issues affecting supervisory decisions
Assess data lineage and its importance for defensible decisions
Evaluate the governance of decision-support systems
Formulate data governance improvements for a sample scenario
syllabus: What data governance means for a supervisory authority
Data ownership, stewardship, and accountability
Data quality dimensions: accuracy, completeness, timeliness
Consequences of poor data governance for supervisory decisions
Facilitated discussion: data quality issues participants have encountered
What data lineage is and why it matters
Tracing a supervisory decision back to its underlying data
Governance of decision-support and analytics systems
Documenting data provenance for audit and challenge
Exercise: trace the data lineage behind a sample supervisory decision
Common data governance weaknesses in supervisory authorities
Practical steps to strengthen data governance
Case study: a decision challenged due to poor data governance
Case study: propose data governance improvements for a sample authority
Recap: governance principles, lineage, applying improvements
Reflection and discussion
Q&A

modules.title: Regulatory Reporting and Data Collection
modules.summary: How authorities design what data they collect, in what form and how often, and the shift from template returns towards granular, standardised and machine-readable reporting.
objectives: Explain the design choices in regulatory reporting frameworks
Assess the costs and benefits of granular and machine-readable reporting
Evaluate validation, quality checks and feedback loops with reporting firms
syllabus: Template returns, granular data and data-pull models
Data standards and identifiers: taxonomies, LEI and common data dictionaries
Validation rules, resubmissions and data quality feedback to firms
Reducing reporting burden while improving supervisory value

modules.title: Interrogating Regulatory Returns
modules.summary: Learn how to interrogate regulatory returns data critically, applying trend analysis and peer comparison rather than accepting figures at face value.
objectives: Apply trend, ratio and peer analysis to regulatory returns
Identify inconsistencies between returns, financial statements and firm narratives
Formulate targeted supervisory questions from return analysis
syllabus: Reading returns critically: what the numbers should and should not show
Trend analysis, ratios and peer group construction
Cross-checking returns against accounts, disclosures and other sources
Exercise: analysing a sample firm's returns and drafting follow-up questions

modules.title: Anomaly Detection, Risk Scoring and Dashboards
modules.summary: How to build and interpret supervisory dashboards, early warning indicators and risk scores that surface anomalies for investigation without creating false confidence.
objectives: Explain the design of early warning indicators and risk scoring models
Evaluate supervisory dashboards for clarity, relevance and decision usefulness
Assess false positives, thresholds and the role of judgement in alerts
syllabus: Early warning indicators and outlier detection techniques
Risk scoring models: weighting, calibration and override
Dashboard design for supervisors and senior management
Exercise: building and critiquing a sample supervisory dashboard

modules.title: Advanced Analytics and AI in Supervision
modules.summary: The use of natural language processing, network analysis and machine learning in supervision, what these techniques add to traditional analysis, and where they fall short.
objectives: Explain how text analytics, network analysis and machine learning are applied in supervision
Evaluate the explainability, bias and validation challenges of supervisory AI
Identify suitable and unsuitable use cases for advanced analytics
syllabus: Natural language processing of documents, returns and complaints
Network analysis of ownership, transactions and interconnectedness
Machine learning and generative AI for supervisory tasks
Explainability, bias and validation of supervisory models

modules.title: SupTech Use Cases Across Supervisory Functions
modules.summary: A tour of SupTech applications across authorisation, ongoing supervision, market surveillance, financial crime and consumer protection, drawing on international case studies.
objectives: Analyse SupTech use cases across the authority's core functions
Evaluate case studies of successful and unsuccessful SupTech projects
Identify use cases with the highest value for the authority
syllabus: Authorisation and fitness and propriety screening
Market surveillance and transaction reporting analytics
Financial crime, AML/CFT risk scoring and sanctions screening
Complaints, web monitoring and consumer harm detection

modules.title: Building the Authority's SupTech Capability
modules.summary: The practical choices involved in building SupTech capability, including build versus buy, public procurement, skills, resourcing and starting with focused pilots.
objectives: Evaluate build-versus-buy and hybrid approaches for SupTech tools
Assess the skills, roles and resourcing needed to sustain SupTech
Identify practical steps for starting or scaling a SupTech programme
syllabus: Build, buy and hybrid models: control, speed, cost and lock-in
Procurement considerations specific to public authorities
Data scientists, data engineers and supervisory translators
Pilots, proofs of concept and scaling what works

modules.title: Governing Supervisory Analytics and the SupTech Roadmap
modules.summary: Brings the programme together into a governance and strategy view of supervisory analytics, including model risk, ethics, information security and a phased roadmap for the authority.
objectives: Explain the governance, model risk and ethical considerations for supervisory analytics
Assess the authority's data and SupTech maturity against its supervisory priorities
Design a phased SupTech and data roadmap
syllabus: Model risk management for the authority's own tools
Confidentiality, information security and cloud use for supervisory data
Change management and embedding analytics in supervisory culture
Workshop: the authority's phased SupTech roadmap

related.title: Applied AI for Supervisory Staff

related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to assess financial crime controls and firms' use of AI in monitoring, screening, fraud and surveillance.
